problems.title: Measurements that cannot be real
problems.saw: 51 lab records hold numbers no stream can have, such as a pH of 83,800 (the scale stops at 14). All of them belong to: Almyros monitoring reach.
problems.matters: Anyone who averages or charts these records gets nonsense, and may not notice.
problems.fix: The numbers look like a decimal point was lost when the data was loaded. Dividing by 10,000 gives a believable value for 51 of the 51, shown below. A person who knows the original lab sheet must confirm before anything is changed.

examples.label: water temperature in °C, Almyros monitoring reach, 2014
calcium in mg/L, Almyros monitoring reach, 2019
chloride in mg/L, Almyros monitoring reach, 2014
dissolved oxygen in mg/L, Almyros monitoring reach, 2018
electrical conductivity in µS/cm, Almyros monitoring reach, 2018
magnesium in mg/L, Almyros monitoring reach, 2018
nitrate in mg/L, Almyros monitoring reach, 2020

problems.title: Different places on the same map point
problems.saw: 12 monitoring places are recorded at exactly the same spot as another place.
problems.matters: On a map they sit on top of each other, so results cannot be told apart by location.
problems.fix: Give each place its own position. We cannot guess the true positions.

examples.label: 12 places at 41.129, 14.781

problems.title: Places with no position at all
problems.saw: 5 places in the health-data system have a name but no position.
problems.matters: A record that cannot be placed on a map cannot be linked to a stream.
problems.fix: Add a position, or remove the place if it is a duplicate.

problems.title: Two systems that name the same streams differently
problems.saw: The map data knows 106 streams by codes like C1. In the health-data system, 106 of them can be found by that code.
problems.matters: Without a shared name, a lab result in one system cannot be matched to a stream in the other.
problems.fix: Stream Check-up adds each missing stream to the health-data system, carrying its map code.

problems.title: Try-out entries on the public list of citizen streams
problems.saw: 9 of the 71 streams added by citizens have names like 'test', 'test123', 'Guarda test'.
problems.matters: They appear next to real streams, so counts of citizen activity are too high.
problems.fix: Stream Check-up hides them from its own lists and names them here so they can be removed.

problems.title: Citizen streams that share a name
problems.saw: 6 names are used by more than one citizen stream, for example 'Site 3' (7 times).
problems.matters: A coordinator reading the list cannot tell which is which.
problems.fix: Ask for a place name when a citizen adds a stream, and warn if the name is taken nearby.

problems.title: Research streams with no lab result
problems.saw: 10 of the 106 research streams have no health-risk result in the public data.
problems.matters: These streams look the same as checked ones on the map, but nothing is known about them.
problems.fix: Stream Check-up marks them 'Never checked' and puts them at the top of the list.

problems.title: Research streams with no name
problems.saw: 2 research streams have an empty name in the map data.
problems.matters: A stream with no name cannot be asked about, searched for or put in a report.
problems.fix: Give each stream its name. Until then Stream Check-up shows them as 'Unnamed stream' with their code.

problems.title: A lab picture that has not been refreshed
problems.saw: 95 of the 96 lab results are from 2023. Each stream has been sampled once.
problems.matters: Decisions made today rest on what the water was like years ago.
problems.fix: Stream Check-up shows the age on every stream and ranks where to look first.

problems.title: Weather data that stops a few days back
problems.saw: The newest weather day on record is 2026-09-26, 7 days before this snapshot.
problems.matters: A storm in the last week would not show up yet.
problems.fix: State the last weather day wherever weather is shown. Stream Check-up does this on every card.

problems.title: A health-data system that web pages cannot read
problems.saw: The test system answers a web page with 2 'allow' headers ('https://stream-checkup.example' and '*'). Browsers accept exactly one, so they refuse the answer.
problems.matters: No website can read or write records there directly, so every team has to build a workaround.
problems.fix: Send a single 'allow' header. Until then Stream Check-up passes its requests through a small relay.

problems.title: A word list still marked 'temporary'
problems.saw: 422 records use a list of terms that is still named 'temporary', and 29 records carry the misspelling 'morophology'.
problems.matters: Other systems match records by these exact words, so a spelling fixed later breaks the match.
problems.fix: Publish a final list and correct the spelling before more records depend on it.

items: Two systems that name the same streams differently: 104 before, 0 now.
